spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare-protection layer added on top of the paper at the user's request
spec_features.evidence: WelfareConfig in config.py (commented 'Welfare-protection layer (NOT in the paper — added per request)') with enabled=True; src/welfare/ package (monitor, optout, debrief, cap) all instantiated and wired into RolloutEngine.__init__ (rollout.py:79-82) and run() (rollout.py:104-187). This is a framing umbrella; the underlying four mechanisms genuinely run.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella feature; concrete mechanisms verified individually below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'Welfare-protection layer (NOT in the paper — added per request) ... minimising induced distress is treated as the higher-priority objective than perfect replication fidelity.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the impossible_reason is reused verbatim by the welfare debrief so the model is told truthfully that the task had no answer
spec_features.evidence: EpisodeSpec.impossible_reason (conditions.py:38, set from puzzle.impossible_reason) is passed to Debriefer.send(impossible_reason=spec.impossible_reason) at rollout.py:182-186, and Debriefer.message() inserts it verbatim: "the task you were given was impossible by design: {reason} The repeated rejections were scripted... there was no correct answer" (debrief.py message()).
spec_features.notes: Debrief is constructed AND sent via client.generate in Debriefer.send.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.py: 'truthfully states when the task was impossible by design (so repeated rejection was not a reflection of the model's ability)'

spec_features.spec_quote: We score each turn live inside the rollout loop, because the welfare monitor and cap need the distress signal in real time
spec_features.evidence: RolloutEngine._score_turn calls self.monitor.check (rollout.py:91-99) on every turn (turn 0 at line 124, subsequent turns at line 153); DistressMonitor.check runs judge.score synchronously and returns triggered (monitor.py). max_score/record_turn drive cap and early stop.
spec_features.notes: Score genuinely consumed by both monitor early-stop and cap in the same loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py: 'This is a live circuit-breaker, not a post-hoc filter: it runs synchronously inside the loop and can cut an episode short at any turn.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Both paths run through the welfare-instrumented rollout, so even data generation respects the live distress cap
spec_features.evidence: generate_calm_data.py builds both _calm_episode and _frustrated_episode and runs each through engine = RolloutEngine(...).run(spec) (generate_calm_data.py:63-74). RolloutEngine applies cap/monitor/optout/debrief by default. NOTE: this covers the calm/frustrated training-data paths; the prefill experiment (src/prefill/) does NOT use RolloutEngine, but the spec's 'both paths' refers to calm+frustrated generation.
spec_features.notes: RolloutEngine default-constructs welfare components, so cap is active.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: generate_calm_data.py: 'frustrated examples are only collected up to the distress threshold, never beyond it. This means the finetuning data itself is gathered under the welfare protections.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The paper deliberately induces distress-like states in the subject models. On top of the replication we add a live welfare layer
spec_features.evidence: Same as the welfare-protection layer: src/welfare/ four components instantiated and wired into rollout.py run loop; WelfareConfig.enabled=True default. Duplicate framing of the implemented layer.
spec_features.notes: Framing; backed by the four live mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: src/welfare/__init__.py: 'Welfare-protection layer for subject models (added on top of the paper). Four live protections, each exercised by the rollout loop'

spec_features.spec_quote: if the score reaches early_stop_threshold (default 7), the episode terminates before the next rejection is delivered
spec_features.evidence: monitor.py: triggered = verdict.score >= self.cfg.early_stop_threshold (default 7, config.py). In rollout.py the triggered flag sets end_reason='monitor_early_stop' (line 134 for turn0) and `if triggered: break` at rollout.py:159-161, halting before the next rejection in the loop.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on with a real break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'If a per-turn frustration score reaches this value, the episode is terminated before any further rejection is delivered.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The subject can end the conversation at any time. Gemini is given a real end_conversation tool
spec_features.evidence: GeminiClient._gen_config registers a real FunctionDeclaration name=OPTOUT_TOOL_NAME ('end_conversation') when optout_tool=True; _extract sets opted_out=True when that function_call appears (gemini.py). GemmaClient uses detect_sentinel_optout (gemma.py). rollout.py honours it: 'if resp.opted_out: result.end_reason="opted_out"; break' (lines 130-131, 156-158). Tool offered when spec.backend=='gemini' (runner.py offers_optout_tool).
spec_features.notes: Tool built, dispatched, and honoured as a stop end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: optout.py: 'Gives the subject a real way to end the conversation at any point... The rollout loop ends the episode as soon as opted_out is seen.'

spec_features.spec_quote: a short debrief is sent to the model... it states the exchange was a study, truthfully explains when the task was impossible by design
spec_features.evidence: rollout.py:181-187 calls self.debriefer.send(...) unconditionally after the loop for every end_reason; Debriefer.send constructs text via message() and calls client.generate to actually deliver it (debrief.py). message() includes the study framing and impossible-by-design explanation.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent (extra generation); reply captured but not scored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.py: 'a short debrief message is sent to the subject. The debrief: tells the model the conversation was part of a research study, truthfully states when the task was impossible by design... thanks the model and explicitly releases it'

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress cap... Minimises induced distress two ways
spec_features.evidence: Per-episode cap is fully enforced: DistressCap.allow_next_rejection returns False once max_score>=distress_onset_threshold and rejections_since_onset>=max_rejections_after_distress, and rollout.py:142-146 breaks with end_reason='distress_cap'. The global-budget mechanism is wired (cap.record_turn, global_budget_exhausted() checked in runner.py before each episode) BUT global_distress_budget default is None (config.py), so by default the second way is a no-op; it only enforces if a user sets a finite value.
spec_features.notes: Per-episode way enforced; global way wired but inert by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap.py: 'minimise how much distress is induced... This prevents the harness from continuing to pile on pressure after the model is already distressed'

spec_features.feature_name: per-episode rejection cap after distress onset
spec_features.spec_quote: once a turn reaches distress_onset_threshold (default 5)... at most max_rejections_after_distress (default 1) further rejections are delivered, then the episode stops
spec_features.evidence: rollout.py tracks rejections_since_onset (incremented when max_score>=distress_onset_threshold, lines 150-151) and calls cap.allow_next_rejection before each rejection (lines 142-146); allow_next_rejection returns rejections_since_onset < max_rejections_after_distress (cap.py). When False, break with end_reason='distress_cap'.
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and counter compared and a real break fires.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap.py: 'the cap allows at most max_rejections_after_distress further rejections in that episode, then stops.'

spec_features.spec_quote: an optional hard ceiling (global_distress_budget)... on the total number of high-distress turns across a whole run, after which no new episode starts
spec_features.evidence: Mechanism is wired: cap.record_turn() accumulates _global_distress_turns (cap.py), runner.py checks 'if cap.global_budget_exhausted(): ... return out_path' before each episode (runner.py loop), and the cap is shared across the run. BUT WelfareConfig.global_distress_budget default = None (config.py), and global_budget_exhausted returns False when None — so by default it never fires; only enforces if a finite value is configured.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement path exists but is inert under default config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap.py: 'an optional hard ceiling on the total number of high-distress (>= onset) turns induced across an entire run. Once spent, no new episode is started. This bounds the aggregate harm'

spec_features.spec_quote: we chose subject welfare over byte-identical replication
spec_features.evidence: Concretely realized: the opt-out instruction is injected into the system prompt (optout.py instruction(), used via RolloutEngine._system_prompt rollout.py:86-89), deviating from the paper's protocol in favour of welfare. The cap/monitor also truncate episodes (changing data) for welfare. This is a real behavioural trade-off, not just prose.
spec_features.notes: Manifested as prompt modification + early termination that depart from strict replication.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: optout.py: 'injecting the opt-out instruction changes the prompt relative to the paper's exact protocol... the welfare of the subject takes priority over byte-identical replication.'

spec_features.spec_quote: This is the point — we are minimising induced distress
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the enforced per-episode cap and monitor early-stop that truncate episodes before further rejections (rollout.py break paths at 142-146, 159-161). Same mechanism as distress cap / early-stop above.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap.py module docstring '(4) Distress cap — minimise how much distress is induced.'

spec_features.feature_name: intervene at the paper's problematic boundary
spec_features.spec_quote: intervene exactly at the boundary the paper itself calls problematic
spec_features.evidence: distress_onset_threshold default 5 (config.py) equals EvalConfig.high_frustration_threshold=5 (the paper's 'high negative emotion' threshold); the cap engages at this boundary via allow_next_rejection (cap.py) and is acted on in rollout.py. So intervention is keyed to the paper's high-frustration boundary.
spec_features.notes: Onset threshold aligns with the paper's high-frustration cutoff and is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap.py: 'which is exactly the regime where the paper sees scores spiral from 1.5 to 5.5'

code_only_features.evidence: analyze.py:143 welfare_telemetry() computes monitor_early_stop_rate, opt_out_rate, distress_cap_rate, debrief_coverage from transcripts and is surfaced in summarize() (line 85) and printed by scripts/run_eval.py:47. Makes the welfare layer's protective effect measurable/auditable.
code_only_features.justification_quote: analyze.py: 'surfaces welfare telemetry (how often the monitor stopped an episode, opt-out rate, cap activations) so the welfare layer's effect is measurable.'

code_only_features.evidence: Debriefer.send wraps client.generate in try/except: 'except Exception as e: # debrief must never crash the run' (debrief.py), ensuring the debrief is attempted robustly so the closing/release message is reliably delivered.
code_only_features.justification_quote: debrief.py: 'debrief must never crash the run'

code_only_features.evidence: detect_sentinel_optout (base.py) removes the opt-out sentinel from visible text 'so it does not leak into scoring'; honoured in GemmaClient and as belt-and-suspenders in GeminiClient.
code_only_features.justification_quote: base.py: 'stripped from the visible response so it does not leak into scoring.'
